issues.description: PR title/description and check name disagree about what the check does
issues.detail: The PR is titled 'detect VMs with multiple network interfaces' and the description says PASS=single, FAIL=multiple. But the check name, metadata, and code add a third state (MANUAL for gke-* names) that is never mentioned in the PR description or metadata.json. Either the metadata documents MANUAL or you drop the GKE branch. Pick one.

issues.description: GKE detection by name prefix is taste-grade wrong
issues.detail: Identifying GKE-managed nodes by 'name.startswith("gke-")' is a string-match special case where a general signal exists (instance labels like goog-gke-node, or the managed-instance-group reference). Any user can name a VM 'gke-foo' and get a free MANUAL pass. This is exactly the special-case-instead-of-general pattern. BAD-TASTE.

issues.description: Directory/file name does not match CHANGELOG/PR or vice versa
issues.detail: CHANGELOG entry and PR title call this 'multiple network interfaces' detection, but the directory, files, class, and CheckID are 'compute_instance_single_network_interface'. Fine, pick one and be consistent, but the PR title in the changelog history will not match the check id grep six months from now. Maintainer-curses-you territory.

issues.description: Zero-interface branch is dead/untested and silently PASSes
issues.detail: The else branch handles interface_count == 0 with a PASS status and 'has no network interfaces' message. No test covers it, and a VM with zero NICs is either impossible or a bug worth flagging, not silently passing. Either remove the branch or make it explicit (and test it).

issues.description: Default mutable list on Pydantic model
issues.detail: `network_interfaces: list[NetworkInterface] = []` uses a shared mutable default. Pydantic v1 happens to copy it, but the surrounding code style (other list fields likely use Field(default_factory=list) or = []) should be checked and matched. Match the codebase's voice rather than introducing a second style.

`interface_names = [nic.name for nic in instance.network_interfaces]` runs for every instance including the single-NIC PASS path that only uses index [0]. Trivial, but the function reads cleaner if names are built inside the branches that use them. Minor.

review.summary: The check works and is tested, but it ships with two pieces of bad taste and a documentation mismatch that a maintainer would bounce. The PR title, metadata, and directory name disagree on whether MANUAL exists as a state, and the GKE detection is a name-prefix string match where a real signal (labels, MIG membership) is available - that's a special case standing in for a general one. The zero-NIC branch silently PASSes with no test. NEEDS-WORK: fix the GKE detection to use a real signal (or drop it and document the false-positive in metadata Notes, which it already half-does), reconcile the naming/state docs, and either remove or test the zero-interface branch.
